digest.component_or_area: CI testing infrastructure, pytest timeout mechanism
propositions: Per-test timeout budget was reduced from 300s to 20s in commit 6a5c88027c5, but legitimate whole-tree-scan tests cost 18.7–29.93s on the covered CI legs, placing the budget inside the band of legitimate costs rather than above it.

With timeout_method=thread, pytest-timeout calls os._exit(1) to kill the xdist worker process instead of reporting a Failed:Timeout verdict, producing zero timeout verdicts and causing worker crashes with zero diagnostic output.

The gating ubuntu-latest py3.13 leg (the only one adding --cov=rebar) experiences 11–14 worker deaths per run because coverage approximately doubles test execution time, pushing legitimate tests against the 20s budget line.

Worker crashes under --dist loadgroup cause the dead worker's pending items to be re-dispatched to respawned workers that die on the same item up to the restart cap, burning job time toward the 60-minute timeout and causing the suite to hang until the job-level cap.

A patchset-only fix to _build-and-test.yml workflow text (e.g., changing --timeout=20 to --timeout=300) is inert on its own Verified gate run because GitHub resolves reusable workflows at the caller's trusted-main commit, not the patchset commit, so main's stale CLI flags override the patchset's ini changes.

Restoring timeout=300 in pyproject.toml and both shared-tier _build-and-test.yml lanes unblocks CI; the budget must carry ~10x headroom above the 29.93s worst-case legitimate test to survive ordinary variance and worker-restart re-payment costs.
